My Idea for the sniping problem is as follows. I suggest that we weight the votes of people. This will make it to where sniping wont make as much as a difference. The Higher up on the All Authors list the more your votes are weighted.
1 - 10 is weighted at 5
11 - 20 at 4
21 - 30 at 3

Judges will be judging on a few things:
Best use of space (duh) X/10 - is the space used wisely and efficiently?
Funness X/10 - how much did you enjoy it?
Asthetics X/10 - Does it look good?
Game play X/10 - Does it all work well?

#11567 1 2006-10-04T04:54:30Z rocket_thumped
The Paradox

The philosopher David Hume enjoyed playing billiards. He was well aware of the fact that when a moving ball strikes a stationary one (event A), the stationary one then starts to move (event B), according to Newton's Law of the Conservation of Energy. We would normally describe this occurrence by saying 'event A causes event B'.

Causality is a concept derived from the principle of induction, according to which we believe that something will happen in the future because it has occurred many times in the past. So we believe that the sun will rise tomorrow, why? Because it has risen many times before. Hume showed that however many times the sun has risen in the past, this does not prove that the sun will rise tomorrow, our belief is just that, a belief.

Going back to our statement 'event A causes event B', the problem is that however many times event B follows event A, it is not possible to say that there is any necessary connection between the two. So it is not valid to say that event A 'causes' event B, that would imply the forbidden necessary connection. All we can say is that in all known instances in the past, event A has been followed by event B. And we can say nothing about the future.

The paradox arises because the whole of science and engineering is based on the principle of causality. Empirically, causality works. Philosophically, it is meaningless.

What is the solution?

When Hume grasped just how paradoxical the concept of causality was, he started to doubt his reason. His reason told him that causality must be true, but his reason also dictated the opposite. To avoid having a nervous breakdown, he dropped the subject, and played billiards all day for nearly two years! This is dangerous territory.

Philosophers from Kant to Popper have tried and failed. Can we succeed?



Reference
David Hume: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding - Section Vll

#11781 1 2006-10-16T17:55:38Z rocket_thumped
I was talking to spect and it seems he feels its a lost cause so I decided to give it a shot. Basicly this time people will sign up to be either a highscorer, a mapmaker or both..(although they will only get picked for one) You will also state wether you will are willing to be a team captain. Then the team captains will draft highscorers and map makers to have a total of 2 highscorers and 2 mapmakers. The 2 mapmakers will each make one map. Then the 2 highscorers from each team highscore all 4 maps and the fastest 4 scores for each team wins the highscoring. The map juding is highlt undecide but I was thinking on a basic scale of 10 in enjoyability. The map makers will have 4 days to make the maps and the highscorers have 3 days to highscore the levels after the submissions of the maps. the teams will get one point for winning the highscore portion and one point for winning the mapmaking portion. The tie breaker is undecided but I was thinking a 10 minute map show down between the teams best mapmakers. The judges are yet to be decided. Any suggestions or comments?

*Rules*
3 people per a team, 1 highscorers and 2 mapmakers.
Each week will infact last a week!
The mapmakers will have 4 days to make their maps.
The highscorers will have 3 days to highscore the maps.
Playable maps only.
Maps must be possible to beat.
Ties will be broken by a ten minute map show down by the two teams best authors.
Demos will be recorded in userlevels form.
If the maps have speacle conditions such as "no jump" or "no left" you need to make it clear.
If you are highscoring a map with a speacle demo you need to abide by those conditions.

#14522 1 2007-03-21T22:35:19Z rocket_thumped
We've all played Prisoner maps before. Anyone that has beaten the game has gone through the utter claustrophobic hell that was 80-1. And after that map, there were many more. The map inspired an entirely new genre of maps. They weren't really puzzle, or action, or race. They were Prisoner maps.
Today is the beginning of a contest that commemorates these bold, fresh, and new maps. Your objective? Make a prisoner map.


THE RULES
-2 maps per person
-Each map has to be a prisoner map
-No old entries. (Like you actually have any.. )

Now, what exactly is a prisoner map you may ask if you are a complete retard that was completely lucky to muster up the ability to stumble upon this forum and read this post? It's simple. At one point or another, the ninja is placed between two drones, and forced around a linear path at the designated speed of the drones. I'm going to be flexible with the definition, because I would love to have some very creative entries. Don't push it, though. I can, and will, disqualify you if your entry simply isn't a prisoner map.


JUDGING
Judging is simple. It will be divided into two categories.

CREATIVITY
10 Points

MAP QUALITY
20 Points

THE JUDGES

rocket_thumped
spiker
lord_day
Demonz

THE PRIZES

1st Place: You get an auto-graph from the wonderful Aju. He's really cool. It's totally worth it.

2nd Place: Some random digital camera I have laying around. Oddly enough, I don't obsessively take pictures of myself, so I don't really need it.

3rd Place: An iPod Nano! It's Apple's pride and joy, and it comes in like, 5 colors. You'll get black if you come in third. No other choices.

And that's it! Let the contest begin...
...Now!

#15024 1 2007-04-29T06:28:21Z rocket_thumped
Sig of the Week

Basically, I will give a theme and maybe some special requirements, then you will enter the sig, that you yourself made, and Ill make a new topic for the members of our wonderful forum to vote on. The winner will then receive a tag stating they won that weeks SOTW (sig of the week). Basically, you will have from Monday to Friday to make a sig and send it to me through PM along with the link to it. Then voting will commence throughout the weekend.

Ill be using a points system also, to see who finish most consecutively and best overall.

1st - 5 points
2nd - 4 points
3rd - 3 points
4th - 2 points
5th - 1 point

The rest of you will get zilch points.
Note: The person with the highest amount of points at the end of the month will get the Sig Maker of the Month Award.

The Rules
1. You must have created the sig your self. No ripping. If you think someone has ripped someone elses sig, PM me with your complaint, be sure to give me a link.

2. You must follow the theme for the week. No exceptions. This is at my discretion.

3. Your sig must not be any bigger than 500 pixels wide and 200 pixels tall.

4. All tie-breakers will be decided by a set panel of 3 people, if they entered a sig and it just so happens to tie, someone else will be substituted in their place.

5. Your sig must be in by Friday of that week. No exceptions.

6. Previously made sigs will not be allowed. This will rely on the honor system, don't be a douche bag.

7. If one sig doesn't get more than half the votes, the best two sigs from the poll will go to a panel of judges.

#331098 5 2007-06-14T06:18:51Z rocket_thumped
It's called clipping masks, if I'm understanding your question correctly.

1. Put the text you want on a new layer.

2. Make that layer invisible.

3. Create a new layer, then apply image. image>apply image (I think)

4. Then press ctrl+alt+g.

5. Make the text layer visible.

6. Move around the clipping masked layer until you get the desired effect.

Quote
It's an old story, we figured. Someone, in a bar somewhere, scribbling on a napkin in the failing afternoon light; the kind of story or list or note that might be crammed in a pocket and pulled out years later to tell something deep and forgotten -- perhaps life's most intimate first chapter, nearly lost forever. So we gave this spontaneous medium a shot. We put 250 napkins in the mail to writers from all over the country -- some with a half dozen books to their name, others just finishing their first. In return, we got nearly a hundred stories. We present most of them here -- from lush to spare, hilarious to terrifying.

Three categories, music and lyrics. Music must be completely instrumental, and preferably streamable. And now an open category with both lyrics and music. Lyrics most be written only. Rules
- 2 Songs per category.
- "Lyric" songs must be written only and "Music" songs must be completely instrumental.
- Deadline is Sept. 29th.

Judging
- I hand selected the Judges in order to achieve a genre balanced panel.
- Entries will be judged from 1 to 10. (This is simple, I know.)
- The back up Judge will judge the judges entries.
- The high and low scores for each entry will be dropped and the remaining scores will be summed.

Judges
- Sept

- Skyline

- Southpaw

Changing Faces

Well, another map pack from the failed project Horizon. There are about 70 something maps, they aren't arranged in episodes at all, but they are roughly arranged by difficulty level. You may see some maps that are suspiciously similar to some on NUMA, that was planed. I was going to do this contest where you had to guess which maps were based on which, but I decided to drop and I had learned to love those maps too much to take them out of the map pack.

lord_day helped playtest, Templex played some of the maps as well. Homunculus is a birthday map for lord_day and a small thank you for his wonderful playtesting.

Enjoy!
